column2: A soprano of the tragic-actress type at the Paris Opéra. She had a great triumph in Piccinni's Didon (1783).
I am rethinking cello fingering from the very beginning.
Let me show you the modern way of playing the cello.
The virtuoso who established modern cello fingering. Napoleon is said later to have borrowed his Stradivari to try it and scratched it with the spur of his boot.
Flute or bassoon — I play both.
A virtuoso of both flute and bassoon, called 'the French Mozart'.
An opera of mine once started a revolution, you know.
I know the art of setting a theatre alight.
In 1830, during a performance of La Muette de Portici in Brussels, the audience rose in revolt: the spark of the Belgian Revolution.
I have my classes at the Conservatoire, you see.
I shall lend you my strength, pupils and all.
Professor at the Paris Conservatoire, teacher of Gounod and Bizet. Bizet later married his daughter.
A ballet? I can write one in a month.
I promise you music one can dance to.
Composer of the ballet Giselle (1841) and of the Christmas carol 'Minuit, chrétiens' (O Holy Night).
Twelve Études in the minor keys
I am not fond of appearing in public.
A friend of Chopin's I can trust.
A pianist of transcendent technique whom even Liszt respected. Extremely unsociable, he lived long as a recluse. He was Chopin's neighbour and close friend.
The same salary as the male professors. That is my condition.

The only woman to hold a full professorship at the Paris Conservatoire in the 19th century (piano, for 30 years from 1842). She fought for the same salary as her male colleagues and won it after the success of her Nonet.
We put gaslight on the stage — and the ghosts of nuns began to dance.
Let us overwhelm them with the sheer scale of grand opera.
Emperor of grand opera at the Paris Opéra. The 'Ballet of the Nuns' in Robert le diable caused a sensation.
I have played before His Majesty Napoleon himself.
A virtuoso who made his name as Napoleon's personal flautist.
Wherever I can be near Maria.
A Belgian violin virtuoso. Lover of the diva Malibran, and later her husband.
The organ of Sainte-Clotilde is waiting for me.
As God wills, I shall lend my strength.
Organist of Sainte-Clotilde. Most of his major works were written after the age of 60. The Violin Sonata was a wedding present for Ysaÿe.
I have a piece I wrote for young Sarasate.
The passion of Spain, for your orchestra.
The Symphonie espagnole (1875) was written for Sarasate. He began as the violist of a string quartet.
I have just given a ballet its premiere at the new Opéra.
Music for dancing? Leave it to me.
With Coppélia and Sylvia he transformed ballet music. Tchaikovsky wrote that after hearing Sylvia he was ashamed of his own Swan Lake.
These are days when even the gods dance the cancan.
Laughter and profit — leave both to me.
King of operetta. In 1876 he toured America. German-born, he was also a cello virtuoso.
I am only just back from London.
Melodies like prayers, for your stage.
Faust (1859) was one of the most performed operas of its time. He is also known for the 'Ave Maria' that lays a melody over a Bach prelude.
Is a sweet melody a sin?
Let us melt the hearts of Paris.
He swept the opera world with his sweet melodies. At the Paris Conservatoire he taught Charpentier among others.
I have choir practice at the Madeleine.

He deputised at the Madeleine for his teacher Saint-Saëns and became choirmaster there in 1877. The First Violin Sonata was completed in 1876 and first performed the following year. He and Saint-Saëns were friends for life.
Do come to my salon again tonight.
With my voice or my connections, I shall help you.
Malibran's sister. As singer, composer and salon hostess she was a pillar of musical Paris. The woman Turgenev loved all his life.
Come and hear the organ of Saint-Sulpice.
The cathedral of the organ, for your orchestra.
Organist of Saint-Sulpice for 64 years from 1870.
The cancan from Offenbach's Orphée aux enfers
Saint-Saëns: 'Le Cygne' from Le Carnaval des animaux
My music may be ignored like the furniture.
Interesting. But I shall bring my umbrella.
A cabaret pianist in Montmartre. In 1905, at 39, he went back to school at the Schola Cantorum. He proposed 'furniture music'.
Symphonie sur un chant montagnard français
I have classes at the Schola Cantorum.
On the teaching of Maître Franck.
Founder of the Schola Cantorum. A leading pupil of Franck, he taught Satie and Roussel.
A piece that is not perfect, I burn.
I promise you one perfect piece.
An extreme perfectionist who destroyed many of his own works late in life. L'Apprenti sorcier later became widely known through a Disney film.
Without discipline there is no freedom.
With my pupils, I shall train your orchestra.
At the 1908 Prix de Rome she caused a stir by submitting an instrumental fugue for the vocal fugue set. She later became the greatest composition teacher of the 20th century.
My sister spoke well of your orchestra.
I want to write while I still can.
In 1913 she became the first woman to win the Prix de Rome grand prize. A pupil of her sister Nadia. Frail from childhood.
I am the only one who can sing Mélisande.
Paris or Chicago, I shall fill the house.
Born in Scotland. In 1902 she created the role of Mélisande at the premiere of Pelléas et Mélisande.
Premiere of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring
However wild the house becomes, I conduct to the end.
Let me lend you a cool baton.
Conductor of the Ballets Russes. In 1913 he conducted the premiere of The Rite of Spring through to the end amid shouting and brawling. Originally a violist.
Maître Fauré's music is in my keeping.
The French piano, for your orchestra.
A great interpreter of Fauré and Ravel. She later gave the premiere of Ravel's Piano Concerto in G.

The real Paganini lost much of his fortune in the failure of the Casino Paganini and died in Nice in 1840.
The real Liszt retired from the concert platform in 1847 and devoted himself to conducting and composing in Weimar. Late in life he took minor orders.
The real Mozart died in Vienna in 1791, aged 35. Still in debt, he was buried in a common grave.
The real Wagner died in Venice in 1883. The Bayreuth Festival is still held every summer.
The real Brahms died in Vienna in 1897, a bachelor to the last, the year after the death of Clara Schumann.
The real Bach died in Leipzig in 1750, and for a time his music was forgotten. It came back to life in 1829, with Mendelssohn's revival of the St Matthew Passion.
The real Handel was nearly ruined by his opera ventures, but rose again with the English oratorio Messiah and was buried in Westminster Abbey.
The real Mahler died in 1911. True to his words 'My time will come', a worldwide Mahler boom arrived about half a century later.
The real R. Strauss lived until 1949 and left the Four Last Songs at the very end of his life.
The orchestra's parts came to rest in an archive, but some 100 years later a young conductor would find the copies and astonish the world.
Later historians of music write that the golden age of Viennese Classicism began with this orchestra.
Afterwards the orchestra toured all over Europe and was called 'the great travelling orchestra of the Romantics'.
Having won the 'War of the Romantics', the orchestra stayed at the centre of the musical world as the century drew to its close.
As the footsteps of the Great War drew near, the orchestra crossed the Atlantic and built the sound of a new age in the New World.
